> High-Performance Robotic Arm The High-Performance Robotic Arm is a 5-DOF robotic system designed to accurately pick up, move, rotate, and place objects. The arm uses five stepper motors to control the base, shoulder, elbow, wrist pitch, and wrist rotation, along with a servo-powered gripper for gripping objects. An ESP32 microcontroller will coordinate the motors and provide precise movement control. Stepper-motor drivers will enable controlled positioning, while limit switches can be used for homing and safety. The mechanical structure will be designed for stability, smooth movement, and reliable operation. The project is designed with future upgrades in mind, including wireless control, programmed movements, sensors, and camera-based object detection. The ultimate goal is to create a strong, precise, and versatile robotic arm that demonstrates practical robotics, electronics, mechanical design, and embedded programming.
